sub_units.name: JSX
sub_units.content: JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It allows us to write HTML in React by converting it into React elements that can be rendered to the DOM. JSX makes it easier to write and add HTML in React.

sub_units.name: Components (Functional/Class)
sub_units.content: Components are the building blocks of any React application. Functional components are simple JavaScript functions that return JSX, while Class components are ES6 classes that extend React.Component. Modern React development primarily uses functional components with hooks.

sub_units.name: Props
sub_units.content: Props (short for properties) are used to pass data from one component to another (primarily from parent to child). They are read-only and help make components reusable and dynamic.

sub_units.name: State
sub_units.content: State is an object that holds information about the component that might change over time. Unlike props, state is managed within the component and can be updated using the useState hook or setState in class components.

sub_units.name: Event Handling
sub_units.content: React events are named using camelCase, such as onClick instead of onclick. Event handlers are passed as functions rather than strings. Understanding how to handle user interactions is fundamental to building interactive UIs.

sub_units.name: Conditional Rendering
sub_units.content: Conditional rendering in React works the same way conditions work in JavaScript. You can use JavaScript operators like if or the ternary operator to create elements representing the current state.

sub_units.name: Lists & Keys
sub_units.content: In React, you can render lists of data using the map() function. Keys help React identify which items have changed, are added, or are removed, giving the elements a stable identity and improving performance.
